title: Traceability link
description: One correspondence between an L2 source element and an L3 output element. The set of links for an artifact is what the round-trip check consumes: every source element maps to exactly one output element and back, with no orphans on either side. Links are also what lets a reviewer ask what a given output came from and get an answer rather than an inference.

kind.description: What kind of L2 element this is.

ref.description: Stable reference: a BPMN element id, a spreadsheet sheet and row, or a data element id such as IMMZ.C.DE1.

label.description: Human-readable label from the source, for reading the link without opening the DAK.

kind.description: What kind of L3 element this is.

ref.description: FHIRPath into the generated resource, or a canonical URL.

derivation.description: derived: mechanically produced from the source with no choice involved. inferred: produced by a rule that could reasonably have gone another way. decided: the source is silent and a person or agent chose. The third category is the one that matters — almost every difference between a generated model and a hand-authored one is a decision the source does not contain, and recording which links are decisions is what makes those differences reviewable instead of mysterious.

rule.description: The transformation rule applied, where the derivation is mechanical.

note.description: Why, when the derivation is inferred or decided. Expected on anything not derived.

flagRef.description: Flag id, where the link is provisional pending someone else's answer.

then.description: A link that is not mechanically derived must say why it is what it is, or the record is no better than no record.

examples.rule: one bpmn:task becomes one PlanDefinition.action, in document order

examples.note: Lane title matched a declared persona by normalised name. The BPMN carries no persona identifier, so the match is by label and could be wrong if two personas share a display name.
